content.purpose: Create another filesystem name or a path reference to an existing file.
content.mentalModel: A hard link is another name for the same inode. A symbolic link is a small object containing a target path and can become dangling.

demonstration.explanation: This small example isolates the main idea behind links.

remember: A hard link is another name for the same inode. A symbolic link is a small object containing a target path and can become dangling.
Verify the resulting state before moving on.

tasks.instruction: Create /home/student/lab/hard-link as a hard link to original.txt and /home/student/lab/symbolic-link as a symbolic link to original.txt.
hints: A copy has different data; the task asks for two kinds of links.
ln creates a hard link by default, and -s creates a symbolic link.
Using a relative symbolic target keeps the link readable inside the same directory.
tasks.suggestedSolution: cd /home/student/lab && ln original.txt hard-link && ln -s original.txt symbolic-link
